    All Classes and Interfaces

    Class
    Description
    AppDataFolder
    Where the Task Manager keeps its data on this computer: the database, for the signed-in Windows user, in %LOCALAPPDATA%\TaskManager.
    DeleteTaskDialog
    Asks before a task is deleted, naming it, since a delete cannot be undone.
    DesktopApp
    The JavaFX application.
    Dialog
    A dialog over the window: its title and note, its fields, and what its buttons do.
    DialogFrame
    What every dialog sits in: the dimmed window, and a white card with the dialog's title, note, fields, the reason a save was refused, and Cancel and the main button at its foot.
    Icons
    The app's icons, drawn from SVG paths on a square of their size: 16px line icons at a 1.5 stroke beside a label, and smaller marks inside controls.
    MainWindowController
    The window, and the one screen in it: the header, which stands in for the system's title bar; the sidebar, with the status filters and their counts, always in view, and the keyboard shortcuts; and the task list, with its heading, the search, and the notice a task that has gone is reported in.
    Refused
    A change the app will not make, and why, in words the screen shows as they are.
    StatusLook
    How a status looks wherever the window shows it, in the design system's states: Pending is neutral, with a dash; In Progress is info, under way, with a clock; Completed is success, with a check.
    Task
    Something the user has to do: a title, a description, how far it has got, and when it was added and last changed.
    TaskCell
    One task in the list, as a row of columns: its title with the first line of its description under it; its status as a tinted pill that opens a menu of the three, so a status is changed straight from the list; when it was last changed, and added; and Edit and Delete, shown while the row is pointed at or chosen.
    TaskCounts
    How many tasks there are in each status, as the counts kept in view show them.
    TaskDialog
    The form a task is added and edited in: its title and description, each with a count of its characters against the limit, and, for a task already saved, its status.
    TaskManagerApplication
    Starts the Task Manager: the class Spring Boot is configured from, and the one the IDE and the Maven wrapper run.
    TaskRepository
    The user's tasks, newest first: all of them, those matching a search, and how many have each status.
    TaskService
    Tasks: adding, listing, changing and deleting them.
    TaskStatus
    How far a task has got.
    TaskText
    The words the task screen puts together from what it shows: a time as the list writes it, the line under the title, what an empty list says, and a count of characters as the form keeps it.
    TaskText.Empty
    What an empty list says.
    Ui
    The pieces the window is built of, styled by taskmanager.css: text, buttons, key caps, fields' labels, and the alert and notice a refusal is shown in.
